paragraphs: Unless otherwise indicated, references to "Dorian," the "Company," "we," "our," "us," or similar terms refer to Dorian LPG Ltd. and its subsidiaries. We use the term "VLGC" to refer to very large gas carriers and "VLGC/AC" to refer to very large gas carriers that are purpose built to transport full ammonia cargoes in addition to LPG. We use the term "LPG" to refer to liquefied petroleum gas and we use the term "cbm" to refer to cubic meters in describing the carrying capacity of our vessels. Unless otherwise indicated, all references to "U.S. dollars," "USD," and "$" in this report are to the lawful currency of the United States of America.

Dorian was incorporated on July 1, 2013 under the laws of the Republic of the Marshall Islands, is headquartered in the United States and is engaged in the transportation of LPG. Specifically, Dorian and its subsidiaries are focused on owning and operating VLGCs in the LPG shipping industry. Our founding executives have managed vessels in the LPG shipping market since 2002. As of May 22, 2026, our fleet consists of twenty-seven VLGCs, including one 93,000 cbm dual-fuel ECO-design Very Large Gas Carrier / Ammonia Carrier ("VLGC/AC"), one 84,000 cbm dual-fuel ECO-design VLGC; eighteen fuel-efficient 84,000 cbm ECO-design VLGCs, or our ECO VLGCs; one 82,000 cbm modern VLGC/AC; four time chartered-in dual fuel Panamax size VLGCs; one time chartered-in ECO Panamax VLGC, and one time chartered-in modern VLGC. The twenty-seven vessels in our fleet, including the six time chartered-in vessels, as of May 22, 2026, have an aggregate carrying capacity of approximately 2.3 million cbm and an average age of 9.6 years. We provide in-house commercial services for all of our vessels, including our vessels deployed in the Helios Pool (defined below), which may also receive commercial management services from MOL Energia (defined below). Excluding our time chartered-in vessels, we provide in-house technical management services for all of our vessels, including our vessels deployed in the Helios Pool.

Currently, sixteen of our ECO VLGCs, including one of our time chartered-in ECO VLGCs, and one of our VLGC/ACs are fitted with scrubbers to reduce sulfur emissions. Vessels fitted with scrubbers allow us to reduce our emissions and to burn less refined fuel, which is frequently cheaper than more refined, lower sulfur grades. When the cost of more refined fuel exceeds that of less refined fuel, we are typically able to earn a higher time charter equivalent ("TCE") for spot voyages and to potentially contract time charters at higher rates compared to vessels without scrubbers. Additionally, one of the chartered-in dual-fuel Panamax size VLGCs is equipped with a shaft generator, which generates additional electricity that can be used to reduce fuel consumption and carbon emissions. Two of our vessels are capable of fully loading ammonia cargoes, and three of our vessels have been fitted to be able to load up to 87% of their cargo capacity with ammonia.

On April 1, 2015, we and MOL Energia Pte. Ltd. ("MOL Energia"), formerly known as Phoenix Tankers Pte. Ltd., a wholly-owned subsidiary of Mitsui OSK Lines Ltd., an unaffiliated third party, began operation of Helios LPG Pool LLC, (the "Helios Pool"), a joint venture owned 50% by us and 50% by MOL Energia. We believe that the operation of certain of our VLGCs in this pool allows us to achieve better market coverage. Vessels entered into the Helios Pool are commercially managed jointly by Dorian LPG (DK) ApS, our wholly-owned subsidiary, and MOL Energia. The members of the Helios Pool share in the net pool revenues generated by the entire group of vessels participating in the pool, weighted according to certain technical vessel characteristics, and net pool revenues are distributed as variable rate time charter hire to each participant. The vessels entered into the Helios Pool may operate either in the spot market, pursuant to contracts of affreightment, or COAs, or on time charters of two years' duration or less. We and MOL Energia have agreed that the Helios Pool will have a right of first refusal to undertake any time charter with an original duration greater than two years. As of May 22, 2026, the Helios Pool operated thirty-one VLGCs, including twenty-seven vessels from our fleet, two MOL Energia vessels and two vessels from another participant.

We and/or our pool managers may not be able to successfully secure employment for our vessels or vessels in the Helios Pool, which could adversely affect our financial condition and results of operations.
We face substantial competition in trying to expand relationships with existing customers and obtain new customers.
Restrictions on VLGC transits and increased toll charges at the Panama Canal may have an adverse effect on our results of operations.
Our indebtedness and financial obligations may adversely affect our operational flexibility and financial condition.
We have and may in the future selectively enter into derivative contracts, which can result in higher than market interest rates and charges against our income.
Investments in forward freight derivative instruments could result in losses.
Because we generate all of our revenues in U.S. dollars but incur a portion of our expenses in other currencies, exchange rate fluctuations could adversely affect our results of operations.
If we fail to manage our growth properly, we may incur significant expenses and losses.

An inability to effectively time investments in and divestments of vessels could prevent the implementation of our business strategy and negatively impact our results of operations and financial condition.
Our directors and officers may in the future hold direct or indirect interests in companies that compete with us.
We may be unable to procure adequate insurance coverage at commercially reasonable rates in the future.
Because we obtain some of our insurance through protection and indemnity associations, we may be required to make additional premium payments.
If we purchase secondhand vessels, we may be exposed to increased costs which could adversely affect our earnings.
Certain shareholders have a substantial ownership stake in us, and their interests could conflict with the interests of our other shareholders.
United States tax authorities could treat us as a "passive foreign investment company," or PFIC, which could have adverse United States federal income tax consequences to United States holders.
We may have to pay tax on United States source shipping income, which would reduce our earnings.
paragraphs: The following risks relate principally to us and our business and the industry in which we operate. Other risks relate principally to the securities markets and ownership of our common shares. Any of the risk factors described below could significantly and negatively affect our business, financial condition and results of operations and our ability to pay dividends, and lower the trading price of our common shares.

The following is a summary of the risk factors you should be aware of before making a decision to invest in our common stock. This summary does not address all the risks we face. Additional discussion of the risks summarized in this risk factor summary, and other risks we face, can be found below in this risk factor section and should be carefully considered, together with other information in this Annual Report and other filings with the Commission, before making an investment decision regarding our common stock.

● We, and the Helios Pool, operate exclusively in the VLGC segment of the LPG shipping industry. Due to the general lack of industry diversification, adverse developments in the VLGC segment of the LPG shipping industry may adversely affect our business, financial condition and operating results.
● Seasonal and other fluctuations in respect of spot market charter rates have had in the past and may have in the future a negative effect on our revenues, results of operations and cash flows.

● We and/or our pool managers may not be able to successfully secure employment for our vessels or vessels in the Helios Pool, which could adversely affect our financial condition and results of operations.
● We face substantial competition in trying to expand relationships with existing and new customers.

paragraphs: You should read the following discussion of our financial condition and results of operations in conjunction with our consolidated financial statements and related notes included herein. Among other things, those financial statements include more detailed information regarding the basis of presentation for the following information. The financial statements have been prepared in accordance with U.S. GAAP and are presented in U.S. dollars unless otherwise indicated. The following discussion contains forward‑looking statements that involve risks and uncertainties. As a result of many factors, such as those set forth under "Item 1A—Risk Factors," "Forward-Looking Statements" and elsewhere in this report, our actual results may differ materially from those anticipated in these forward‑looking statements.

We are a Marshall Islands corporation, headquartered in the United States, focused on owning and operating VLGCs. As of May 22, 2026, our fleet consists of twenty-seven VLGCs, including one dual-fuel ECO-design Very Large Gas Carrier / Ammonia Carrier ("VLGC/AC"), one dual-fuel ECO-design VLGC; eighteen fuel-efficient 84,000 cbm ECO-design VLGCs, or our ECO VLGCs; one 82,000 cbm modern VLGC/AC; four time chartered-in dual fuel Panamax size VLGCs; one time chartered-in ECO Panamax VLGC, and one time chartered-in modern VLGC.

On April 1, 2015, Dorian and MOL Energia began operations of the Helios Pool, which entered into pool participation agreements for the purpose of establishing and operating, as charterer, under a variable rate time charter to be entered into with owners or disponent owners of VLGCs, a commercial pool of VLGCs whereby revenues and expenses are shared. The vessels entered into the Helios Pool may operate either in the spot market, pursuant to COAs or on time charters of two years' duration or less (unless agreed otherwise). As of May 22, 2026, all twenty-seven of our VLGCs, including the six time chartered-in vessels, were deployed in the Helios Pool.

Our customers, either directly or through the Helios Pool, include or have included global energy companies such as Exxon Mobil Corp., Chevron Corp., China International United Petroleum & Chemicals Co., Ltd., Royal Dutch Shell plc, Equinor ASA, Total S.A., and Sunoco LP, commodity traders such as Glencore plc, Itochu Corporation, Bayegan Group, Gunvor Group, and the Vitol Group and importers such as E1 Corp., Indian Oil Corporation, SK Gas Co. Ltd., and Astomos Energy Corporation, or subsidiaries of the foregoing. For the year ended March 31, 2026, the Helios Pool accounted for 99% of our total revenues. No other individual charterer accounted for more than 10% of our total revenues. Within the Helios Pool, no individual charterer represented more than 10% of net pool revenues—related party. For the year ended March 31, 2025, the Helios Pool accounted for 97% of our total revenues. No other individual charterer accounted for more than 10% of our total revenues. Within the Helios Pool, one charterer represented more than 10% of net pool revenues—related party. For the year ended March 31, 2024, the Helios Pool accounted for 95% of our total revenues. No other individual charterer accounted for more than 10% of our total revenues. Within the Helios Pool, two charterers each represented more than 10% of net pool revenues—related party. See "Item 1A. Risk Factors—We operate exclusively in the LPG shipping industry. Due to the general lack of industry diversification, adverse developments in the LPG shipping industry may adversely affect our business, financial condition and operating results" and "Item 1A. Risk Factors—We expect to be dependent on a limited number of customers for a material part of our revenues, and failure of such customers to meet their obligations could cause us to suffer losses or negatively impact our results of operations and cash flows."

We continue to pursue a balanced chartering strategy by employing our vessels on a mix of multi-year time charters, some of which may include a profit-sharing component, shorter-term time charters, spot market voyages and COAs. None of our vessels is currently on a fixed time charter outside of the Helios Pool. See "Item 1. Business—Our Fleet" above for more information.

On April 29, 2026, our Board of Directors, on the recommendation of its Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee, unanimously authorized the increase in the size of the Board of Directors from eight to nine directors, and, to fill the resulting vacancy, appointed Christopher Wiernicki to serve as a Class I director, effective immediately.

On April 20, 2026, we prepaid $16.5 million of the 2023 A&R Debt Facility, a proportion related to the 2015-built VLGC Cobra. On May, 6, 2026, we completed the sale of this vessel, receiving proceeds net of commission and fees of $81.9 million.

On May 7, 2026, we announced that our Board of Directors has declared an irregular cash dividend of $1.00 per share of the Company's common stock totaling $42.8 million. The dividend is payable on or about May 28, 2026 to all shareholders of record as of the close of business on May 18, 2026.

We seek to employ our vessels in a manner that maximizes fleet availability and earnings upside through our chartering strategy in line with our goal of maximizing shareholder value and returning capital to shareholders when appropriate, taking into account fluctuations in freight rates in the market and our own views on the direction of those rates in the future. As of May 22, 2026, all twenty-seven of our VLGCs, including the six time chartered-in vessels, were employed in the Helios Pool, which includes time charters with a term of less than two years unless otherwise agreed.

A spot market voyage charter is generally a contract to carry a specific cargo from a load port to a discharge port for an agreed upon freight per ton of cargo or a specified total amount. Under spot market voyage charters, we pay voyage expenses such as port and fuel costs. A time charter is generally a contract to charter a vessel for a fixed period of time at a set daily or monthly rate. Under time charters, the charterer pays voyage expenses such as port and fuel costs. Vessels operating on time charters provide more predictable cash flows, but can yield lower profits than vessels operating in the spot market during periods characterized by favorable market conditions. Vessels operating in the spot market generate revenues that are less predictable but may enable us to capture increased profits during periods of improvements in the freight market although we are exposed to the risk of a decline in the freight market and lower vessel availability. Pools generally consist of a number of vessels which may be owned by a number of different ship owners which operate as a single marketing entity in an effort to produce freight efficiencies. Pools typically employ experienced commercial charterers and operators who have close working relationships with customers and brokers while technical management is typically the responsibility of each ship owner. Under pool arrangements, vessels typically enter the pool under a time charter agreement whereby the cost of bunkers and port expenses are borne by the charterer (i.e., the pool) and operating costs, including crews, maintenance and insurance are typically paid by the owner of the vessel. Pools, in return, typically negotiate charters with customers primarily in the spot market. Since the members of a pool typically share in the revenue generated by the entire group of vessels in the pool, and since pools operate primarily in the spot market, including the pool in which we participate, the revenue earned by vessels placed in spot market related pools is subject to the fluctuations of the spot market and the ability of the pool manager to effectively employ its fleet. We believe that vessel pools can provide cost-effective commercial management activities for a group of similar class vessels and potentially result in lower waiting times and higher earnings.

Contracts of Affreightment relate to the carriage of multiple cargoes over the same or several routes at pre-agreed terms, volumes and periods and enables the COA holder to nominate and lift cargoes, without controlling tonnage themselves or having their own vessel in position. COAs are usually based on voyage terms, where all of the vessel's operating, voyage and capital costs are borne by the ship owner.

On April 1, 2015, Dorian and MOL Energia began operation of the Helios Pool, which is a pool of VLGC vessels. We believe that the operation of certain of our VLGCs in this pool allows us to achieve better market coverage. Vessels entered into the Helios Pool are commercially managed jointly by Dorian LPG (DK) ApS, our wholly-owned subsidiary, and MOL Energia. The members of the Helios Pool share in the net pool revenues generated by the entire group of vessels in the pool, weighted according to certain technical vessel characteristics, and net pool revenues (see Note 2 to our consolidated financial statements included herein) are distributed as variable rate time charter hire to each participant. The vessels entered into the Helios Pool may operate either in the spot market, COAs, or on time charters of two years' duration or less. As of May 22, 2026, the Helios Pool operated thirty-one VLGCs, including all twenty-seven vessels from our fleet, two MOL Energia vessels, and two vessels from another pool participants.

paragraphs: 除非另有說明，文中所稱「Dorian」、「公司」、「我們」、「我們的」、「我們」或類似詞彙，均指 Dorian LPG Ltd. 及其子公司。我們使用「VLGC」一詞來指稱非常大型氣體運輸船，並使用「VLGC/AC」一詞來指稱專門設計用以運輸滿載液氨貨物及液化石油氣的非常大型氣體運輸船。我們使用「LPG」一詞來指稱液化石油氣，並使用「cbm」一詞來描述我們船舶的載貨能力。除非另有說明，文中所有提及「美國美元」、「USD」及「$」均指美國聯邦政府所發行的法定貨幣。

Dorian 於 2013 年 7 月 1 日根據馬紹爾羣島共和國法律設立，總部設於美國，從事液化石油氣的運輸業務。具體而言，Dorian 及其子公司專注於擁有並營運 VLGCs 的液化石油氣運輸產業。我們的創始管理層自 2002 年起便管理液化石油氣運輸市場的船舶。截至 2026 年 5 月 22 日，我們的船隊包含二十七艘 VLGCs，包括一艘 93,000 cbm 雙燃料 ECO 設計非常大型氣體運輸船 / 液氨運輸船（「VLGC/AC」），一艘 84,000 cbm 雙燃料 ECO 設計 VLGC；十八艘節能 84,000 cbm ECO 設計 VLGCs，即我們的 ECO VLGCs；一艘 82,000 cbm 現代 VLGC/AC；四艘租賃進的雙燃料 Panamax 尺寸 VLGCs；一艘租賃進的 ECO Panamax VLGC，以及一艘租賃進的現代 VLGC。截至 2026 年 5 月 22 日，我們船隊中的二十七艘船舶，包括六艘租賃進的船舶，總載貨能力約為 2.3 百萬 cbm，平均船齡為 9.6 年。我們為所有船舶提供內部商業服務，包括我們部署在 Helios Pool（定義如下）的船舶，這些船舶也可能從 MOL Energia（定義如下）獲得商業管理服務。不計我們租賃進的船舶，我們為所有船舶提供內部技術管理服務，包括我們部署在 Helios Pool 的船舶。

目前，我們的十六艘 ECO VLGCs，包括一艘租賃進的 ECO VLGCs，以及一艘 VLGC/AC 已安裝除硫設備以減少硫氧化物排放。安裝除硫設備的船舶使我們能夠減少排放，並減少使用精煉燃料，而精煉燃料通常比更精煉、更低硫含量的等級更便宜。當更精煉燃料的成本高於較不精煉燃料時，我們通常能為即時航程獲得更高的時間租賃等價（「TCE」），並有潛力以較高價格簽訂時間租賃合約，與未安裝除硫設備的船舶相比。此外，一艘租賃進的雙燃料 Panamax 尺寸 VLGC 已安裝軸發電機，可產生額外電力，用以減少燃料消耗及碳排放。我們的兩艘船舶可完全裝載液氨貨物，三艘船舶已安裝以能裝載其載貨能力的 87% 液氨。

我們與 MOL Energia Pte. Ltd.（「MOL Energia」），原為 Phoenix Tankers Pte. Ltd.，為 Mitsui OSK Lines Ltd. 的全資子公司，為無關第三方，於 2015 年 4 月 1 日開始運作 Helios LPG Pool LLC（「Helios Pool」），為一合資公司，由我們與 MOL Energia 各擁有 50%。我們認為，我們部分 VLGCs 在此池中運作，使我們能獲得更好的市場覆蓋。加入 Helios Pool 的船舶由 Dorian LPG (DK) ApS，我們的全資子公司，與 MOL Energia 共同進行商業管理。Helios Pool 的成員根據某些技術船舶特徵，按比例分享整個參與池船舶產生的淨池收入，並以變動率時間租賃費用形式分配給各參與者。加入 Helios Pool 的船舶可於即時市場運作，根據運費合約（COAs）或運輸合約（COAs）或兩年或以下的時間租賃合約運作。我們與 MOL Energia 同意，Helios Pool 對於任何原始持續時間超過兩年的時間租賃，享有優先承購權。截至 2026 年 5 月 22 日，Helios Pool 運作三十一艘 VLGCs，包括我們船隊的二十七艘船舶、兩艘 MOL Energia 船舶及兩艘來自其他參與者的船舶。

paragraphs: 您應配合本公司的合併財務報表及其相關附註，閱讀下列關於我們財務狀況與營運成果的討論。這些財務報表包含有關下列資訊之呈列基礎的更詳細資訊。財務報表係依照美國會計準則（U.S. GAAP）編製，以美元為計價單位，除非另有說明。下列討論包含風險與不確定性之向前看聲明。由於許多因素，例如於「項目 1A—風險因素」、「向前看聲明」及其他處所述，我們實際結果可能與這些向前看聲明所預期者有重大差異。

本公司為馬紹爾羣島公司，總部設於美國，專注於擁有並營運超大型液化氣運輸船（VLGCs）。截至2026年5月22日，本公司船隊包含二十七艘VLGCs，包括一艘雙燃料ECO設計超大型氣體運輸船/氨氣運輸船（"VLGC/AC"），一艘雙燃料ECO設計VLGC；十八艘節能84,000 cbm ECO設計VLGCs，或稱為ECO VLGCs；一艘82,000 cbm現代VLGC/AC；四艘租賃進來的雙燃料巴拿馬級VLGCs；一艘租賃進來的ECO巴拿馬級VLGC，以及一艘租賃進來的現代VLGC。

2015年4月1日，Dorian與MOL Energia開始運作Helios Pool，該池與其他VLGCs的所有人或實際所有人簽訂池參與協議，目的是在變動租賃率時間租賃下，作為租賃人，建立並運作VLGCs之商業池，使收入與費用共享。進入Helios Pool之船舶可於散裝市場運作，依COAs或於兩年或更短時間租賃下運作（除非另有協議）。截至2026年5月22日，本公司所有二十七艘VLGCs，包括六艘租賃進來之船舶，均已部署於Helios Pool中。

我們的客戶，無論直接或透過Helios Pool，包括或曾包括全球能源公司如Exxon Mobil Corp.、Chevron Corp.、中國國際聯合石油化學有限公司、Royal Dutch Shell plc、Equinor ASA、Total S.A.、Sunoco LP，商品經紀商如Glencore plc、Itochu Corporation、Bayegan Group、Gunvor Group、Vitol Group，以及進口商如E1 Corp.、印度石油公司、SK Gas Co. Ltd.、Astonos Energy Corporation，或前述公司的子公司。截至2026年3月31日財年，Helios Pool佔我們總營收的99%。沒有其他個別租賃人佔我們總營收的10%以上。在Helios Pool內，沒有個別租賃人代表淨池營收的10%以上（相關當事人）。截至2025年3月31日財年，Helios Pool佔我們總營收的97%。沒有其他個別租賃人佔我們總營收的10%以上。在Helios Pool內，有一個租賃人代表淨池營收的10%以上（相關當事人）。截至2024年3月31日財年，Helios Pool佔我們總營收的95%。沒有其他個別租賃人佔我們總營收的10%以上。在Helios Pool內，有兩個租賃人各自代表淨池營收的10%以上（相關當事人）。請參閱「項目 1A. 風險因素—我們專門從事LPG運輸產業。由於產業缺乏多元化，LPG運輸產業的不利發展可能對我們的業務、財務狀況與營運成果產生負面影響」及「項目 1A. 風險因素—我們預期將依賴有限數量的客戶來產生我們營收的重要部分，若這些客戶未能履行其義務，可能會導致我們遭受損失或對我們的營運成果與現金流產生負面影響」。
我們持續追求平衡的租賃策略，透過將船舶以多種長期時間租賃、部分可能包含利潤分享零組件、短期時間租賃、散裝市場航程及COAs混合方式運用。目前我們的船舶均未在Helios Pool以外的固定時間租賃下運作。請參閱上方「項目 1. 事業—我們的船隊」以取得更多資訊。
2026年4月29日，本公司董事會根據其提名及企業治理委員會的建議，一致通過將董事會規模從八名董事增至九名董事，並為補缺之職位任命Christopher Wiernicki擔任Class I董事，立即生效。
2026年4月20日，我們預付2023年A&R債務融資2023 A&R Debt Facility的16.5百萬美元，與2015年建造的VLGC Cobra有關。2026年5月6日，我們完成出售此船舶，淨收入（扣除佣金及費用）為81.9百萬美元。
2026年5月7日，我們宣佈本公司董事會已宣佈不尋常現金股息，每股普通股為1.00美元，總計42.8百萬美元。此股息於2026年5月28日或附近日期支付給2026年5月18日收市時登記為本公司股東之所有股東。

我們致力於以能最大化船隊可用性及獲利潛力的方式運用我們的船舶，透過我們的租賃策略，符合我們最大化股東價值及在適當時候回饋資本給股東的目標，同時考量市場 freight rate 的波動以及我們對這些 rate 未來走向的看法。截至 2026 年 5 月 22 日，我們所有二十七艘 VLGC 船隻，包括六艘時間租賃進來的船舶，均在 Helios Pool 中運作，該 Pool 包含時間租賃合約，除非另有協議，否則合約期限均為少於兩年。

一般而言，散裝市場航程租賃是一種合同，用於運輸特定貨物從裝貨港至卸貨港，按每噸貨物協議 freight 或指定總金額計算。在散裝市場航程租賃下，我們支付航程費用，如港口和燃料成本。時間租賃則是一種合同，用於租賃船舶一段固定時間，按每日或每月固定金額計算。在時間租賃下，租賃人支付航程費用，如港口和燃料成本。運行於時間租賃的船舶能提供更可預測的現金流，但在市場條件有利的時期，其獲利可能低於運行於散裝市場的船舶。運行於散裝市場的船舶產生的收入較不穩定，但在 freight 市場改善期間，可能使我們能捕捉更高的獲利，儘管我們面臨 freight 市場下降和船舶可用性降低的風險。Pools 通常由數艘船舶組成，這些船舶可能由不同船東所有，並作為單一市場實體運作，以產生 freight 效率。Pools 通常聘請經驗豐富的商業租賃人和運營者，與客戶和經紀人有緊密的合作關係，而技術管理則通常由各船東負責。在 Pool 安排下，船舶通常以時間租賃合約加入 Pool，其中 bunkers 和港口費用由租賃人（即 Pool）承擔，而運營費用，包括船員、維護和保險，則通常由船舶所有者支付。Pools 通常會與客戶洽談租賃，主要在散裝市場進行。由於 Pool 成員通常會分享 Pool 內所有船舶產生的整體收入，且 Pool 主要在散裝市場運作，包括我們參與的 Pool，因此運行於散裝市場相關 Pool 的船舶所產生的收入會受到散裝市場波動的影響，以及 Pool 管理者有效運用船隊的能力影響。我們認為船舶 Pool 可為一組相似類型的船舶提供成本效益的商業管理活動，並可能導致較短的等待時間和更高的獲利。
Contracts of Affreightment 關係到在相同或數個航線，按預先協議的條件、貨量和期間運輸多種貨物，並使 COA 持有人能指定並裝載貨物，而不必自己控制貨量或擁有船舶在場。COAs 通常基於航程條款，其中船舶的所有運營、航程和資本成本均由船東承擔。

2015 年 4 月 1 日，Dorian 和 MOL Energia 開始運作 Helios Pool，這是一個 VLGC 船隻的 Pool。我們認為，我們部分 VLGC 船隻在這個 Pool 中運作，使我們能獲得更好的市場覆蓋。加入 Helios Pool 的船舶由 Dorian LPG (DK) ApS，我們的全資子公司，和 MOL Energia 共同商業管理。Helios Pool 的成員根據某些技術船舶特性，按比例分享 Pool 內所有船舶產生的淨 Pool 收入，淨 Pool 收入（請參閱本文所附財務報表之附註 2）以變動率時間租賃費用的形式分發給各參與者。加入 Helios Pool 的船舶可能在散裝市場、COAs 或兩年或更短時間租賃下運作。截至 2026 年 5 月 22 日，Helios Pool 運作三十一艘 VLGC，包括我們全部二十七艘船舶，兩艘 MOL Energia 船舶，以及兩艘來自另一 Pool 參與者的船舶。

headings: 散裝貨運市場即時租賃率的季節性及其他波動，過去曾對我們的營業收入、營運結果及現金流產生負面影響，未來亦可能產生相同影響。
本公司及/或我們的船隊經理人可能無法成功為我們的船舶或赫利奧斯船隊的船舶取得船員，這可能會對我們的財務狀況及營運結果產生不利影響。
我們在拓展現有客戶關係及獲得新客戶方面面臨重大競爭。
對 VLGC 船隻通航的限制及巴拿馬運河通行費的增加，可能會對我們的營運結果產生不利影響。
我們的負債及財務義務可能對我們的營運彈性及財務狀況產生不利影響。
我們已並可能在未來選擇性地訂立衍生合約，這可能會導致高於市場利率及對我們收入的費用。
投資於遠期貨運衍生工具可能導致虧損。
因為我們所有的營業收入均以美金計價，但部分費用是以其他貨幣計價，匯率波動可能會對我們的營運成果產生不利影響。
若我們未能妥善管理成長，可能會產生重大費用與虧損。
若無法有效掌握投資與出售船舶的時機，可能會阻礙我們業務策略的執行，並對營運成果與財務狀況產生負面影響。
我們的董事與高階管理人員未來可能直接或間接持有與我們競爭之公司的股權。
我們未來可能無法以商業合理價格取得足夠的保險保障。
因為我們部分保險是透過保護與賠償協會取得，我們可能需要支付額外的保費。
若我們購入二手船舶，可能會面臨增加的成本，這可能會對我們的獲利產生不利影響。
某些股東持有我們相當大的股權，其利益可能與其他股東的利益產生衝突。
美國稅務機關可能將我們視為「被動外國投資公司」，或 PFIC，這可能會對美國持有人造成不利的美國聯邦所得稅後果。
我們可能必須就美國來源的運輸收入納稅，這將降低我們的盈餘。
paragraphs: 下列風險主要與本公司及其業務與所從事產業有關。其他風險則主要與證券市場及本公司普通股之持有相關。任何上述風險因素均可能顯著且負面地影響本公司業務、財務狀況與營運成果，並影響本公司支付股息之能力，同時降低本公司普通股之交易價格。
下列為您在決定投資本公司普通股前應留意之風險因素摘要。此摘要並未涵蓋本公司所面臨之所有風險。有關本風險因素摘要中所提及風險之進一步討論，以及其他本公司所面臨之風險，可於本風險因素節中找到，應與本年度報告及其他向委員會提交之文件資訊一併審慎考量，以作為投資本公司普通股之決策依據。
